prompt:
A clever hand-drawn editorial timeline illustration in the style of a refined illustrated atlas plate: subtle paper grain, fine linework, flat-but-textured shapes, muted natural palette, calm and understated. National Geographic editorial infographic sensibility.

SCENE — two parallel horizontal timelines across the frame, like two lanes, each with three stations above small year labels.

TOP LANE, a little planter figure seen from a slight distance:
- station 1 (label 1962): a young person in simple work clothes standing on sandy ground holding a small sapling.
- station 2 (label 1990): the same figure, now old, walking away with a wave, leaving the frame.
- station 3 (label 2004): the lane is empty, only a small marker post.

BOTTOM LANE, a tree:
- station 1 (label 1962): a tiny sapling in dry ochre sandy ground.
- station 2 (label 1990): a slim half-grown GREEN conifer, maybe shoulder-height to a person.
- station 3 (label 2004): a tall mature GREEN larch, reaching high, full crown, next to a tiny distant figure for scale.

The visual idea: the person's lane ends just as the tree's lane keeps going — by the time the tree is tall, the planter is gone. Ground color transitions from ochre sand on the left to green forest floor on the right. Larch is GREEN throughout; only the distant grassland is ochre. It is early October.

TEXT — render exactly these year labels in a small clean sans-serif: 1962, 1990, 2004 (numbers only, six labels total). Nothing else.

NEGATIVE INSTRUCTIONS — no Chinese characters, no other numbers, letters, words, titles, captions, legends, arrows with text, watermarks, logos, brand marks, English words, faces in close-up, or golden autumn foliage. The larches must be green.
